scenario_information.scenario_description: Windows purple-team breach-and-attack-simulation of the wetland lab TTPs (github.com/s4nntysec/wetland). Each inject reproduces one technique as a self-cleaning PowerShell payload, tagged WETLAND-LAB and mapped to ATT&CK: masquerade as svchost (T1036), scheduled-task + Run-key persistence (T1053.005 / T1547.001), hidden file + timestomp (T1564.001 / T1070.006), an HTTP-shaped C2 beacon (T1071.001 / T1571), and a BENIGN ingress tool-transfer test that downloads the EICAR AV test file via curl.exe (T1105). The techniques are intentionally loud and reversible — the goal is detectable telemetry, not a real implant. Target your Windows assets, run, then review prevention/detection. Edit the beacon's $C2 line.

scenario_injects.inject_title: Ingress Tool Transfer — pull the wld tool onto the host (T1105)
scenario_injects.inject_description: First step of the chain: fetch the tool-under-test. curl.exe downloads wld-windows-x86_64.exe from the v0.1.0 GitHub Release, saves it as wld.exe, verifies it (SHA256 + file size) and runs `wld -h` (benign — prints usage) to prove download+execute, then cleanup removes it. Detection: curl.exe writing wld.exe to disk and a new process spawning from it (proxy/NDR tool transfer; EDR exec-after-download).

Write-Output 'WETLAND-LAB masquerade: cleaned'

injector_contract_payload.command_content:
$ErrorActionPreference='SilentlyContinue'
$dst = Join-Path $env:APPDATA '.wetland-lab.bin'

attrib +h $dst
$ref = Get-Item (Join-Path $env:SystemRoot 'System32\kernel32.dll')
